claims.text: At stage-1 DonHangApp.build creates an ApiClient (each time DonHangApp builds, once in a normal run) and passes it to ProductListScreen; ProductListScreen passes widget.apiClient to LoginScreen, and LoginScreen passes it to CreateOrderScreen.
In _LoginScreenState, _loading and _error are fields changed only through setState and read only by that State's build (spinner on the button, red error text).

ApiClient.login stores the token in the private field _token of the shared ApiClient; createOrder sends it through _headers as Authorization: Bearer; ApiClient has no public member that reports whether a token is set.
In Dart, an identifier starting with an underscore is private to its library, so screens in other files cannot read ApiClient._token.
claims.source_hint: Dart language tour: Libraries and imports / privacy (dart.dev)

claims.text: After login, LoginScreen calls Navigator.pushReplacement: CreateOrderScreen replaces the sign-in route, whose _LoginScreenState (with _loading, _error) is discarded; the order screen's back button returns to ProductListScreen.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: NavigatorState.pushReplacement, State.dispose, AppBar.automaticallyImplyLeading; login_screen.dart:31-33

claims.text: ProductListScreen's app bar always shows the Icons.login button that pushes a new LoginScreen; nothing in its build depends on the token, so after sign-in it shows the same icon.
Assigning to a field or variable does not make any widget build again; Flutter rebuilds a State after setState (or a dependency change), and login calls no setState in ProductListScreen's State.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: State.setState; frontend.l1.setstate-and-rebuilding summary lines 1-2

claims.text: A Dart top-level variable (outside any class or function) whose name does not start with _ and that is neither final nor const can be read and assigned from every file that imports its file.
claims.source_hint: Dart language tour: Variables (top-level variables), Libraries and imports

claims.text: Flutter docs: ephemeral state can be kept in one widget because nothing else needs it; app state is shared across parts of the app (login info is an example); there is no clear-cut rule between them.
Keep state ephemeral while one widget is its only reader; sharing it app-wide lets it outlive its screen and be changed by unrelated screens.
claims.source_hint: outline misconception 1; Flutter docs ephemeral vs app state ('no clear-cut rule')

claims.text: The order screen shows 'Place an order' with an 'Order 1 keyboard' button; the product list's sign-in control is an icon at the top right of the app bar.
After sign-in and going back, the token is still in the one ApiClient the order screen used: nothing in the stage-1 app clears _token (setToken is never called).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: api_client.dart:14-16, 43; git grep setToken (no callers)

claims.text: ProductListScreen receives its constructor arguments once, when DonHangApp builds it as home at app start; a value that appears after sign-in cannot reach it through that constructor.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: main.dart:21; Flutter API docs: Widget (immutable configuration), State.widget
